first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because a friend married on Corfu. The first screen is calm: areas, guest numbers, the view. Nothing shouting. She kept going. Her summary: only Corfu Holiday Palace and Angsana publish anything near our numbers, the only true private hire is The Courti Estate with nine bedrooms and no event capacity, and nobody says whether a resort can be closed. I read the exclusive-use paragraph and the Corfu Imperial entry myself.

journey.quote: The right area depends on how many guests you are inviting, the kind of ceremony you want and the view you want behind you when you say your vows.
journey.reaction: Guest numbers first. Good. It is not trying to sell me a sunset in the first line.

journey.quote: Exclusive use means different things here, from a privately hired estate such as The Courti Estate to Atlantica's promise of one wedding on your day, so ask each venue which one it is offering.
journey.reaction: This is exactly the distinction most people blur. One wedding a day is not a closed property, and they say so. I trust that.

journey.quote: Guest count narrows the list quickly, because published ceremony spaces run from the couple and eight guests at Atlantica's Secret Garden to 250 at Angsana Corfu's Vertigo Sky Bar.
journey.reaction: So the ceiling for a ceremony on this island, as published, is 250. My assistant flagged this straight away. Corfu may be too small for us unless someone knows more than the websites say.

journey.quote: Rooms matter more than usual when most guests fly long-haul from Australia.
journey.reaction: The point about housing everyone is right. The assumption about where my guests fly from is not. We are Dubai, London and Sydney.

journey.quote: At Atlantica Grand Mediterraneo it means the resort hosts only one wedding on your chosen day, not that the resort closes to other guests.
journey.reaction: Plainly said. It saves my assistant a wasted call.

journey.quote: If you are weighing a resort package against a venue on its own terms, our guide to [Greece wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages) sets out how they compare.
journey.reaction: A link to packages in the middle of the exclusive-use discussion. That is the moment I feel filed under standard client.

journey.quote: The Palazzo Imperiale sleeps eight and occupies a small private peninsula within the resort, described as "ideal for total exclusivity".
journey.reaction: Now we are talking. A private peninsula for my parents. This is the line my assistant would send to my mother.

journey.quote: The two named capacities top out at 50, so for a larger guest list ask what Yali holds before you shortlist.
journey.reaction: The most beautiful place on the page, and it stops at 50. Honest, but it leaves my real question open.

journey.quote: With 225 rooms on site, Eva Palace is the Kommeno option for housing a large guest list in one place.
journey.reaction: Useful. 225 rooms is close to our numbers. If it could be closed, it becomes interesting.

journey.quote: **Standout:** The coordinators also help with hair, spa treatments, flowers, photography, decoration and hen and stag nights.
journey.reaction: Hen and stag nights. Not written for me. My assistant would skip this entry.

journey.quote: This is the venue on the list for a guest count in the hundreds with an indoor fallback already built in.
journey.reaction: A clear recommendation at my scale, said quietly. But a ballroom in a town hotel is not what a family like mine pictures for Corfu, and there is nothing on who else is in the hotel.

journey.quote: **House rules as published:** Outdoor receptions start from 20:30, and outdoor music stops at 23:30, after which the party can move indoors to the main restaurant until 04:00 at the latest.
journey.reaction: Real detail. This is what my events team would ask on the first call, and it is already here.

journey.quote: With nine bedrooms, the house holds the wedding party, and most guests will stay nearby.
journey.reaction: The only place that is truly ours, and it sleeps the wedding party. Where do 300 guests go, and who controls who comes up the drive?

journey.quote: **Standout:** Every wedding package includes a personal wedding planner from the resort.
journey.reaction: 'Every wedding package' as the standout. It is accurate, but it reads like a tier list, and it is for a venue that tops out at 30.

journey.section: Getting to Corfu for your wedding
journey.quote: Its [official website](https://www.cfu-airport.gr/en) lists three ways to and from the terminal: by car with GPS directions, by public bus on a direct service, and by taxi.
journey.reaction: A public bus and GPS directions. Nothing on private cars, meet-and-greet or private aviation. My assistant would not forward this section.

journey.section: Getting to Corfu for your wedding
journey.quote: Worth repeating to anyone planning a swim before the welcome drinks.
journey.reaction: Friendly, but it is the tone of a travel blog, not of someone I would hand a 300-guest wedding to.

journey.quote: For a summer date, that means a shaded ceremony spot, a later start, water for guests and an indoor or covered fallback agreed with the venue in advance.
journey.reaction: Wildfire and heat said without drama, with a plan. My security team would want this, and it is not hidden.

journey.quote: **Proving you are free to marry.** As at November 2026, Smartraveller says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most often with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and registry certificates.
journey.reaction: Our lawyers handle this, and we are not only Australian. Skipped.

journey.section: Shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The next step is finding out which of them are free on your date, on your terms.
journey.reaction: 'On your terms' is the right note. Understated, not eager.

journey.section: Shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person start to finish is what I want. 'For Australian couples' tells me, in the last paragraph, that this service may not be for my family.

unanswered_questions: Can Eva Palace or Corfu Imperial be closed to the public for three days or more for a guest list of 200 to 400?
What does the Yali Waterfront Restaurant hold, and can it be combined with other Corfu Imperial spaces for a larger event?
What is the event capacity at The Courti Estate, and how would guests staying elsewhere be moved and screened?
Can private cars, VIP arrivals at Corfu Airport and private aviation be arranged instead of buses and taxis?
Can our own security team work alongside the venue's, and how are vendors and guest photography handled for privacy?
Can several ceremonies and family customs run across a multi-day celebration at one of these venues?
Have they delivered a wedding of 200 to 400 guests on Corfu, and is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: **Standout:** Every wedding package includes a personal wedding planner from the resort.
turn_offs_found.why: Making 'every wedding package' the standout of a venue entry, alongside the 'resort package' link in the exclusive-use section, frames the island as tiers to choose from. That is how a standard client is treated, which is my main fear.

turn_offs_found.quote: Worth repeating to anyone planning a swim before the welcome drinks.
turn_offs_found.why: A chatty safety tip about swimming, after a public bus and GPS directions, pitches the travel section at an ordinary holidaymaker and says nothing about private logistics, which is what I would judge a planner on.

would_share_with: My assistant, to approach Eva Palace and Corfu Imperial about full closure, Yali's capacity and combined spaces
My mother, for the Palazzo Imperiale as a private family base

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=corfu-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet, with no prices or 'value' talk, which I prefer. But I don't fill in web forms, the page says the service is for Australian couples, and nothing shows they have done my scale. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: Rebalance the 'Getting to Corfu' section away from public options (public bus, GPS directions, the swimming aside) towards private logistics: private cars, meet-and-greet at arrivals, private aviation, if true.
Soften the Australia-only framing ('for Australian couples', 'fly long-haul from Australia') in at least one place so families flying from elsewhere still feel addressed.

Thin the package wording where it adds nothing: drop 'Every wedding package includes' as Atlantica's standout, and move the 'resort package' link out of the exclusive-use paragraph so that section reads as options, not tiers.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, cares about scale, closure, security and discretion)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; every turn-off has a why
Title, deferred business details (fees, Wedded Privileges, company specifics) and absent prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing lines

assumptions: Layla is considering Corfu for a 200 to 400 guest wedding; the persona card doesn't name a destination.
Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour.
